text: Refactoring is the process of improving the internal structure of your code without changing what it does on the outside. The main goal is to make the code cleaner, more readable, and easier to maintain in the long run. You might rename confusing variables, break a long function into smaller parts, or remove duplicated logic. Crucially, the program's behavior must stay exactly the same. Over time, if we skip refactoring, we build up "technical debt" – that is, messy code that becomes harder and more expensive to update. By regularly cleaning up our code, we save future time and effort, making our work more enjoyable and efficient.
